target.title: feat(feeds): search and follow signed publisher feeds
target.body:
## Summary

- verify standard DSSE publisher snapshot, query, change, and reset projections without treating discovery data as an install catalog
- fetch bounded same-origin signed pages with revision, cursor, expiry, count, redirect, SSRF, content-type, timeout, and size enforcement
- apply complete change ranges atomically and persist accepted publisher state in SQLite
- persist followed publishers and refresh them through the verified snapshot/delta/reset path
- add `openclaw publisher search|follow|unfollow|list|refresh` as the first complete user-facing publisher-feed workflow

## Context

This is the first independently usable OpenClaw publisher-feed consumer. It now contains the former verifier, transport, durable-refresh, and local-follow slices (#109340, #109378, and #109397) as one vertical review unit.

That consolidation is required by production dead-code enforcement: each lower-level module becomes live only when the registered publisher CLI consumes the follow service. Gateway scheduling/RPCs remain a separate second wave in #109461.

## Stack

Foundation:
- #110037 standard DSSE envelopes with bounded beta compatibility

Producer dependencies:
- openclaw/clawhub#3116
- openclaw/clawhub#3117
- openclaw/clawhub#3005
- openclaw/rfcs#39

Follow-up:
- #109461 gateway scheduling and publisher follow RPCs
- #109584 Control UI and signed-profile selection

## Validation

- focused envelope, projection, transport, durable-state, refresh, follow-store/service, and CLI tests: 44 passed across 8 files
- scoped type-aware `oxlint` across 21 changed TypeScript files
- scoped `oxfmt --check`
- `git diff --check`
- DSSE and transport fixture test-type failures from the first ready runs were fixed and propagated
- production imports now terminate at the registered `publisher` search/follow CLI, eliminating the intermediate dead-code boundary

Fresh automatic CI owns repository-wide test-type and dead-code validation; no jobs were manually queued.
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
A user can search a signed publisher feed, follow it, read the durable follow state, and refresh it through the registered `openclaw publisher` CLI commands.

Real environment tested:
Windows 11 source checkout at exact OpenClaw head `998d9d2628b` under Node 24.15.0. ClawHub #3117 production `signFeedPayload` and publisher projection schemas emitted standard DSSE envelopes under an ephemeral Ed25519 key. OpenClaw used its registered Commander CLI handlers, production verifier/transport parsing, and real SQLite follow and publisher-state stores. The source harness replaced only HTTP fetch with an explicit in-memory response mock.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Generated an ephemeral Ed25519 key and configured a signed `https://clawhub.ai` proof profile in a disposable `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
2. Ran `openclaw publisher search publishers:alice "CUDA Helper" --feed-profile proof --kind skill --limit 10 --json`.
3. Ran `openclaw publisher follow publishers:alice --feed-profile proof --json`.
4. Ran `openclaw publisher list --json`.
5. Ran `openclaw publisher refresh publishers:alice --feed-profile proof --json`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
search:  feedId=clawhub.publisher.publishers:alice sequence=7 entry=skills:cuda-helper signedBy=clawhub-proof-2026-q3 signatureCount=1 threshold=1
follow:  status=initialized publisherId=publishers:alice sequence=7 displayName="Alice GPU Tools"
list:    acceptedSequence=7 displayName="Alice GPU Tools" verifiedAt=2026-07-19T01:31:57.020Z
refresh: ok=true status=unchanged sequence=7 signedBy=clawhub-proof-2026-q3 verifiedAt=2026-07-19T01:31:57.034Z
```
The full JSON transcript showed the normalized query `{ text: "CUDA Helper", kinds: ["skill"] }`, the signed CUDA Helper entry, the persisted follow record, and the subsequent signed no-change delta.

Observed result after fix:
All four registered CLI paths completed successfully. Signature verification identified the ephemeral key, follow initialized a durable sequence-7 snapshot, a separate list command read that SQLite state, and refresh accepted a signed sequence-7 no-change projection as `unchanged`.

What was not tested:
A deployed ClawHub/Convex publisher endpoint was not available. HTTP transport was explicitly mocked in the source harness; DSSE production signing, schema validation, OpenClaw verification, CLI command registration, and SQLite persistence were real.
